reviews.title: very good, pricey with limits
reviews.text:
I really like Rosebud and actually think the AI journaling experience is excellent, especially the Dig Deeper feature and the ability to customize what the AI pays attention to. That’s why I upgraded from the free trial, then to Thrive 2x, and ultimately paid $59.99/month for Thrive 5x.

The problem is that I reached my entire weekly AI usage limit after roughly a day or two of use.

I use journaling conversationally and tend to talk through things in detail. I did not realize that longer Dig Deeper conversations consume progressively more of the weekly allowance, or that users are apparently better off ending an entry and starting a new one to conserve usage. That should be explained much more clearly before someone pays for the highest-tier plan.

I really want to keep using Rosebud because the actual product is great, but $59.99/month is difficult to justify if a heavy conversational user can exhaust the highest plan’s weekly AI allowance that quickly.

I’ve contacted support and would really appreciate clarification on how much Dig Deeper usage Thrive 5x is realistically designed to provide.

Great app and concept, but the pricing and AI usage limitations need much better transparency.

reviews.title: More than just a journaling app - it guided my self love journey
reviews.text:
I don’t write reviews often, but Rosebud deserves a serious one.

I started using this app during one of the most difficult and transformative periods of my life. Within a relatively short amount of time, I experienced major losses and changes in both my personal life and career, while also trying to be present for my family, figure out what came next professionally, and rebuild parts of myself that I hadn’t realized needed rebuilding.

What has surprised me most about Rosebud is that it doesn’t feel like I’m simply typing into a journal and closing it afterward. It helps me actually process what I’m saying. It notices themes, asks thoughtful follow-up questions, connects things I may not have connected on my own, and sometimes puts language to an emotion or pattern that I knew was there but couldn’t quite explain.

There have been entries where I’ve written from a place of frustration, grief, fear, jealousy, hope, excitement, or complete uncertainty, and Rosebud has helped me look at those feelings with more perspective instead of simply getting swallowed by them. I especially appreciate that the reflections don’t always feel like empty reassurance. Some of the most meaningful moments have been when it has gently made me consider another interpretation of something or recognize what may actually be underneath the emotion I’m feeling.

One of my favorite parts has been being able to look back over time. When you’re changing slowly, it can be almost impossible to recognize your own progress while you’re living it. Rosebud has given me a record of that progress. I can look back at what I was worried about, what I believed about myself, what I was trying to survive, and what I hoped would happen—and then compare that person with where I am now. There are things I handle differently today that I probably wouldn’t have even noticed without having those conversations documented.

It has also helped me become much more intentional about self-care and self-love. Not in the superficial sense of forcing myself to “think positive,” but in learning to notice my own behavior, understand why certain things affect me so strongly, acknowledge when I’m actually doing well, and give myself credit for small changes that eventually become meaningful ones.

Rosebud hasn’t magically made difficult things easy, and I actually think that is part of why I value it so much. It hasn’t erased grief, uncertainty, or hard days. Instead, it has helped me understand what I’m going through while I’m going through it. That distinction matters.

There have been nights where I opened the app thinking I was going to write a few sentences and ended up realizing something genuinely important about myself.

Months from now, I know I’m going to be incredibly grateful that I have this record—not only of what happened during this chapter of my life, but of who I was becoming throughout it.

If you are someone who wants more from journaling than simply documenting your day, especially if you’re trying to understand yourself, recognize patterns, work through a period of change, or become more intentional about the person you’re becoming, I genuinely recommend Rosebud.

It has become one of the most meaningful tools I’ve given myself during a very complicated chapter of my life, and I’m genuinely grateful it exists.

reviews.title: Paywalls ruin the experience!!!
reviews.text:
The Good:
When it works, Rosebud has a lot going for it. The concept of an interactive, AI-driven journal that helps synthesize your raw thoughts into meaningful psychological insights, daily goal trackers, and custom reflection cards (like connecting emotional overwhelm to therapeutic frameworks) is genuinely powerful. For anyone who struggles with staring at a blank page or pulling actionable habits out of a chaotic day, the initial experience feels smooth, supportive, and deeply clarifying.

The Catch / The Bad:
Unfortunately, the user experience falls apart when it comes to subscription transparency and usage limits. After signing up for a paid tier (such as the Bloom plan), users may quickly find themselves hitting aggressive, restrictive background limits that drain their monthly allocation within a couple of weeks—or even after just a single deep conversation. Instead of providing a reliable space to process thoughts, the app frequently hits you with walls demanding further upgrades to higher tiers (like Thrive 2x or 5x) just to keep using the features you are already paying for.

The Verdict:
Rosebud has a brilliant core idea, but the execution of its pricing structure and hidden usage caps makes it feel less like a supportive wellness tool and more like a meter running out. If you don't want to worry about rationing your thoughts or feeling like you’re getting locked out of your own account mid-month, it's hard to justify the cost. Not worth it!

reviews.title: Very helpful to see patterns
reviews.text: I started using Rosebud when I was noticing toxic patterns my partner and I were stuck in. I have a therapist, he has a therapist, we had a couples therapist too. I started using Rosebud and putting in incidences and things my partner was saying to me. Rosebud was able to point out that things were really not good, even though I was hearing that from friends, my therapist, and eventually the couples therapist. It wasn’t until I saw everything typed out and Rosebud picking up on toxic patterns that I was able to really see my partner was a complete narcissist and I was being emotionally abused. It’s funny that this app was what opened my eyes and not all the humans in my life, but it is what it is. I find the app helpful for recognizing patterns in myself too and helping me stick to my boundaries. I am happy to report I’m free of that relationship that wasn’t serving me. I’m healthier and happier!
